stance_basis: letter calls for stronger noise standards and public hearing provisions before final regulations are issued
summary: John E. Hirten, as Assistant Secretary for Environment and Urban Systems (Designate) at the Office of the Secretary of Transportation, submitted a letter reviewing the proposed regulations and draft EIS on off-road vehicle use on public lands. His primary concern was that the noise regulation section was inadequate, noting that state regulations may be non-existent or inadequate, and he suggested the final regulations include discussion of public hearings and a mechanism for handling complaints about noise, pollution, and destruction.
complaint_summary: Hirten's letter raises three concerns: the noise regulation section needs stronger standards (since state regulations may be non-existent or inadequate), the final regulations should include provisions for public hearings on area/trail designations, and a mechanism for handling complaints about noise, pollution, and destruction should be established.

statement.text:
This office has reviewed the proposed regulations and the draft environmental impact statement concerning the use of off-road vehicles on public lands managed by bureaus of the Department of the Interior.
Our primary concern is with the sections covering regulation of noise emitted by these vehicles. It is stated that a vehicle which produces unusual or excessive noise or other pollutants shall not be permitted to operate on public lands. A statement on the need to develop appropriate noise standards would strengthen this section, as State regulations may be either non-existent or inadequate in some instances.
We suggest that the final regulations include discussion of the opportunity for public hearings with respect to designation of areas and trails for the use of off-road vehicles. If such hearings are anticipated, are environmental impact statements to be prepared in advance of these hearings in order to evaluate the environmental effects of off-road vehicles? Is there currently a mechanism set up for handling complaints because of noise, pollution, or other destruction to public lands or wildlife on the part of vehicles or their operators?

We hope these comments will be of some assistance to you, and we look forward to receiving the Department of the Interior's final regulations and the final environmental impact statement on the operation of off-road vehicles on public lands.
Sincerely yours,
John E. Hirten
Assistant Secretary for
XIATINE
Environment and Urban Systems
(Designate)
